input_signals.name: Persistent Cash Profit Buyback Confirmation
input_signals.hypothesis: Net repurchases are most bullish when executed by firms with persistently high operating cash flow profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: A buyback by a cash-generative firm is more likely to reflect undervaluation or disciplined capital allocation than financial engineering. Scaling net repurchases by assets and interacting them with smoothed cash profitability targets firms where financing actions confirm underlying quality.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), rank( ratio( sub( prstkc, sstk ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Retained Earnings Dilution Trap
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(ib, at), 3), RATIO(re, at)))), RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity issuance is most bearish when done by firms with weak profitability and poor accumulated retained earnings.
input_signals.reasoning: Low retained earnings and weak earnings profitability indicate limited internally generated capital and lower firm quality. When such firms issue equity, the action may reveal overvaluation, distress financing, or dilution risk rather than valuable growth investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( sumrank( ma( ratio( ib, at ), 3 ), ratio( re, at ) ) ) ), rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Gross Profit Deterioration Security Issuer
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5))), RANK(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: External security issuance is most bearish when operating gross profitability is deteriorating.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the mechanical accrual-minus-net-financing pairing by using a real-activity quality measure, gross profit scaled by assets, and gross external funding rather than net payout. Issuance by firms with weakening gross profitability is more likely to reflect adverse-selection financing, overvaluation, or funding pressure than value-creating investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( trend( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 5 ) ) ), rank( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Weak Cash Debt Funded Payout
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))), RANK(MIN(RATIO(dltis, at), RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Debt-funded payouts are bearish when undertaken by firms with weak operating cash-flow quality.
input_signals.reasoning: Simultaneous borrowing and shareholder distributions can indicate financial engineering or an unsustainable payout policy. The negative implication should be strongest when operating cash flow is weak, because the payout is less likely to be internally funded and more likely to increase future financing strain.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ), rank( min( ratio( dltis, at ), ratio( add( prstkc, dvc ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Weak Cash Dual Issuer
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), RATIO(re, at)))), RANK(MIN(RATIO(sstk, at), RATIO(dltis, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Simultaneous equity and debt issuance is most bearish when firms have weak cash generation and poor accumulated profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: The MIN construction targets firms tapping both major external capital markets rather than simply issuing one security. When that dual financing need is paired with low operating cash flow and weak retained earnings, it is more likely to reveal funding stress or overvaluation than productive investment demand.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( sumrank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ), ratio( re, at ) ) ) ), rank( min( ratio( sstk, at ), ratio( dltis, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Quality Deleveraging Buyback
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), RATIO(re, at))), RANK(MIN(RATIO(prstkc, at), RATIO(NEG(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Repurchases are most bullish when high-quality firms are also reducing debt.
input_signals.reasoning: A buyback accompanied by balance-sheet deleveraging is less likely to be debt-financed financial engineering. When paired with persistent cash generation and strong retained earnings, the financing action more plausibly signals undervaluation and disciplined capital allocation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( sumrank( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ), ratio( re, at ) ) ), rank( min( ratio( prstkc, at ), ratio( neg( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ) ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Low Retention Equity Financing
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity issuance is most bearish when the firm has a weak retained-earnings base relative to its asset scale.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids another operating-efficiency deterioration trend and instead focuses on the balance-sheet quality of internally accumulated capital. Scaling stock issuance by assets plus the absolute retained-earnings base emphasizes firms raising equity despite little internally generated capital cushion, where issuance is more likely to signal dilution, overvaluation, or financing dependence.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( ratio( re, at ) ) ), rank( ratio( sstk, add( abs( re ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Weak Cash Net Equity Reversal
input_signals.hypothesis: A shift toward net equity issuance is bearish when firms have weak persistent operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids split-contaminated share-count growth by using dollar issuance and repurchase flows. A worsening net equity financing position is more informative when internal cash generation is weak, suggesting dilution or funding pressure rather than opportunistic capital structure management.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ), rank( delta( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Maintenance Burden Debt Issuer
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(WINSOR(RATIO(dp, sale), 1), NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)))), RANK(RATIO(dltis, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Debt issuance is most bearish when firms have high asset-maintenance burden and weak cash-flow quality.
input_signals.reasoning: High depreciation relative to sales proxies for a capital-intensive operating base that may require continuing reinvestment just to maintain capacity. If such firms also have weak operating cash flow and issue debt, the financing action is more likely to fund maintenance strain than value-creating growth.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( sumrank( winsor( ratio( dp, sale ), 1 ), neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) ), rank( ratio( dltis, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Equity Issuer Unsupported Dividend
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)), MUL(RANK(RATIO(dvc, at)), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity issuance is most bearish when firms with weak operating cash generation are still paying sizable cash dividends.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the prior MIN-scale problem by requiring high ranked equity issuance, high ranked dividends, and weak cash-flow quality rather than letting the smaller dividend leg dominate mechanically. The mechanism is that equity issuance while maintaining dividends under poor internal cash generation signals dilution, payout-smoothing pressure, or catering rather than genuine financial strength.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ), mul( rank( ratio( dvc, at ) ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Quality Liquidity Term Out
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(act, lct), MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))), RANK(MIN(RATIO(dltis, at), RATIO(NEG(DELTA(dlc, 1)), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Replacing short-term debt with long-term debt is bullish when supported by strong liquidity and operating cash-flow quality.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from the distressed equity-issuance channel and tests a maturity-management mechanism: long-term debt issuance paired with current-debt reduction. For firms with good liquidity and cash generation, terming out debt likely reduces rollover risk and confirms financing flexibility rather than distress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( sumrank( ratio( act, lct ), ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ), rank( min( ratio( dltis, at ), ratio( neg( delta( dlc, 1 ) ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Weak Cash Dividend Instability Issuer
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3))), MUL(RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)), RANK(ABS(DELTA(RATIO(dvc, at), 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity issuance is most bearish when weak-cash-flow firms also show unstable dividend policy.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids treating dividend cuts as bullish by using the absolute dividend change, so both cuts and unsupported increases are interpreted as policy instability when paired with weak cash generation. The signal targets firms issuing equity while dividend policy is under strain, consistent with dilution, catering, or funding pressure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ), mul( rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ), rank( abs( delta( ratio( dvc, at ), 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Deterioration Payout Withdrawal
input_signals.hypothesis: Payout reductions are bearish when firms are also experiencing deteriorating operating cash-flow quality.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids another retained-earnings-plus-equity-issuance construction and instead studies withdrawal of shareholder distributions as the financing action. Falling repurchases or dividends may be a particularly negative confirmation signal when cash-flow quality is already deteriorating, consistent with funding stress rather than prudent flexibility.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( trend( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) ), rank( neg( delta( ratio( add( prstkc, dvc ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: External Funding Payout Retrenchment
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at)), MUL(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at), 1))), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: External financing is most bearish when firms are cutting shareholder payouts while operating cash-flow quality is deteriorating.
input_signals.reasoning: This fixes the prior scale mismatch by ranking the external-financing level and payout-change legs separately rather than combining them through MIN. The signal requires three aligned stress signals: outside financing, payout retrenchment, and declining cash-flow quality.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ) ), mul( rank( neg( delta( ratio( add( prstkc, dvc ), at ), 1 ) ) ), rank( neg( trend( ratio( oancf, at ), 5 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Unproductive Asset Expansion Funder
input_signals.hypothesis: External financing is bearish when it funds asset growth that is not matched by sales growth.
input_signals.reasoning: Asset expansion is lower quality when the asset base grows faster than revenue, suggesting declining productivity or low-return investment. If that expansion is paired with equity or debt issuance, the financing action may reveal overinvestment or funding dependence rather than valuable growth.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( sub( rank( growth( at, 1 ) ), rank( growth( sale, 1 ) ) ) ), rank( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Gross Profit Drawdown Security Issuer
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5), RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at))), RANK(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Security issuance is bearish when gross profitability has fallen far below its own recent peak.
input_signals.reasoning: This measures a profitability drawdown rather than a simple linear trend, focusing on firms that have materially deteriorated from a recent operating-quality high. External financing during such a drawdown may be more likely to reflect adverse selection or funding stress than investment in high-quality growth.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( sub( ts_max( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 5 ), ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ) ) ), rank( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Dividend Burden Net Equity Funder
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(dvt, ADD(ABS(oancf), dp)), 1)), RANK(SUB(RANK(RATIO(sstk, at)), RANK(RATIO(prstkc, at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Net equity issuance is bearish when firms carry a high dividend burden relative to internal cash-generation capacity.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the short-debt dividend-strain family and instead asks whether dividends look externally supported through the equity channel. A high dividend burden relative to operating cash flow plus depreciation, paired with equity issuance rather than repurchase, is more consistent with dilution-funded payout maintenance than durable quality.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( winsor( ratio( dvt, add( abs( oancf ), dp ) ), 1 ) ), rank( sub( rank( ratio( sstk, at ) ), rank( ratio( prstkc, at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: External Funding After Dividend Stop
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(sstk, dltis), at)), MUL(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(dvc, at), 1))), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: External financing is bearish when weak-cash-flow firms cut dividends.
input_signals.reasoning: This removes the lagged near-duplicate structure and isolates a cleaner dividend-distress channel rather than broad payout retrenchment. A dividend cut combined with weak cash generation and outside financing is a stronger sign of funding stress than either the cut or financing action alone.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( add( sstk, dltis ), at ) ), mul( rank( neg( delta( ratio( dvc, at ), 1 ) ) ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ) ) ) )
